title: RBAC Template Factory and Policy Primer for Private VPC Deployments
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (RBAC Template Factory) and accompanying policy primer that generates least-privilege IAM role and policy artifacts for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The module must support: (1) scoped service roles for agent/daemon/service-controller components, (2) customer-assumable cross-account roles for upgrades and telemetry (opt-in), (3) management of permission boundaries and role tagging conventions, and (4) automated health-check accounts/roles used by the upgrade controller. Deliverables: a published internal Terraform module, a concise policy primer with decision rationale, automated integration tests (terraform-compliance + AWS IAM simulator smoke tests), and a rollout plan for using the module in new and existing customer private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry with semantic versioning and CHANGELOG
Module exposes variables for role name prefix, service scope, permission boundary ARN, and allow-list of actions per component
Default policy sets implement least privilege for: control-plane-controller, kv-cache-sync, model-fetcher, metrics-prober, and upgrade-runner
Module supports 'assume_role_map' JSON input to create cross-account assume roles with external_id patterns
Automated CI covers: plan-only drift detection on a representative private deployment fixture and policy Simulator runs for each generated role
Security sign-off from security team recorded in PR before v1.0.0 release
implementation_notes: We will follow a composition-first module pattern: variables + policy templates + role factory to allow customers to opt-in/out of default policies.
Policy templates will be generated using HCL templates (terraform's templatefile) not inline long strings; easier to review diffs and reuse snippets.
Use permission boundaries as recommended: default to a Redwood-managed boundary ARN variable but allow overriding with customer's KMS-backed boundary.
Avoid broad wildcard actions. For S3, use GetObject/ListBucket with resource-level ARNs. For KMS, require kms:Decrypt only when model key is referenced.
Provide an escape hatch 'breakglass' role pattern that requires multi-owner approval recorded in audit logs (implementation via a flag that creates a role with MFA + approval policy document).
design_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: single monolithic module vs set of small composable modules. Chosen: small composable modules (role-factory, policy-templates, assume-role) to make reuse easier across private + dedicated products.
Tradeoff: strict enforced permission boundary by default vs safer opt-in. Chosen: enable permissive boundary variable but set conservative default and require explicit override to relax.
Tradeoff: encode allow-lists in module vs external policy store. Chosen: provide sane defaults in module and point to an external policy repo for customer-specific overrides to speed onboarding.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): publish module v0.1.0 to internal registry; test against dev private cluster fixtures; gather telemetry on plan/apply times
Phase 2 (pilot customers): onboard 2 small customers through Solutions Eng using module with per-customer overrides; collect feedback and missing permission cases
Phase 3 (widen): release v1.0.0 after security sign-off; update onboarding docs and console templates to use new role names/ARNs
Phase 4 (retrofit): run automated migration playbook for ~10 pilot private deployments; provide a migration script that creates new role, performs canary-assume tests, then flips service to new role
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + tfsec baseline on module

Integration: spawn ephemeral AWS accounts with mock-private-deploy fixture, run terraform apply (using the module) and perform the following checks: role assume test, policy simulator run for representative API calls, permission boundary enforcement test
Regression: add terraform-compliance scenarios to CI to detect accidental wildcard permissions
Monitoring: add a periodic CI job that runs 'terraform plan' against a canonical private-deploy state file to detect drift after module changes
